text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high error rate & cross-region latency spike detected for requests from APAC -> EU model pool. auto-threshold tripped: 5m error rate = 6.8% (baseline 0.2%) · probing telemetry shows region-pin mismatch for certain tenants. paging oncall (maria)

maria: saw the page, jumping in. quick ask: is this ongoing for all APAC or subset of customers? any customer-facing errors?

chen: I'm seeing a surge of 502/503 from edge proxies in ap-southeast1 that are routed to eu-west1 pools. latencies in traces: 300-800ms extra plus retries. looks like routing policy version v23.4.1 applied at 08:12 UTC rolled to a subset of routers.

adarsh: confirmed: rollout of policy v23.4.1 included a new latency-based fallback that incorrectly prefers eu-west1 for routes tagged with region:ap-southeast. logs show policy evaluation returned "preferred_region: eu-west1" for keys that should have been sticky to ap-southeast1.

lee: adding networking context — our geo-dns TTL was 300s but we had short-term caching anomalies in CDN layer; some nodes still had old pins. combination of mis-evaluation + stale pins = repeated cross-region pins.

ops-bot: NOTE: customer-impact classification: P1-degraded (high error rate for ~12k requests/min from APAC), alert routed to #incidents and #eng-sre.

maria: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause policy rollout / rollback to v23.4.0 2) force pin override for affected tenant prefixes to ap-southeast1 3) reduce DNS TTL to 30s for region pins 4) monitor errors and latency. assigning actions — chen/adarsh handle rollback + override, lee handle TTL change, sophia to message CS about impacted customers.

chen: running rollback now — pausing rollout in router-control plane: `POST /api/v1/router/policy/rollout/pause?v=23.4.1` -> response 202 accepted.

adarsh: applying immediate pin override script for prefixes matching `tenant: (acme|beta-inc|edge-saas)` — running:

```
# apply region override
curl -XPOST "https://control-plane.internal/pins/override" -d '{"prefixes": ["tenant:acme","tenant:beta-inc","tenant:edge-saas"], "region":"ap-southeast1", "ttl": 120}
' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```

-> returns 200 for first batch, queued for async propagation.

lee: changing DNS TTL for pins -> 300s -> 30s across ap-southeast1 edge zone, pushing via dns-admin: `dnsctl set-ttl pin.apac.redwood 30` — propagation starting.

sophia: contacting Customer Success lead @sophia -> updating status doc: "We observed elevated errors for customers routed from APAC to EU due to a buggy routing policy rollout; immediate rollbacks and region overrides applied. No data loss. We'll follow up with root cause and ETA to re-enable safe rollout." sending to top 10 impacted accounts now.

ops-bot: automation note: Canary watchers disabled for v23.4.1. Re-evaluating rollout gating.

maria: initial telemetry after rollback + override: error rate falling from 6.8% -> 1.2% in 2 mins, median latency for APAC flows dropped ~260ms. still seeing tail errors on ~2% of requests.

chen: digging into router logs: we saw evaluation cache not respecting tenant pin annotations when policy rule included remote-latency-weight. reproduced locally: when rule contains `fallback: latency` and `pin_annotation` present, evaluation engine chooses fallback region due to ordering bug. code path hit in evaluation_v2. patch ready (PR #9082) to fix ordering.

adarsh: will hold v23.4.1 rollout until PR merged and canary proves clean. we should also add a unit/regression test for pin+latency interactions.

lee: DNS TTL change propagated to ~80% of nodes within 90s. nodes that still had old TTL are being actively flushed by CDN purge.

maria: can we get a quick customer impact summary for post-incident triage? sophia?

sophia: quick numbers from dash: impacted requests ~720k over 14m window; peak impacted accounts ~12 (top 3 saw >10% of their requests affected), no billing anomalies reported, no data integrity issues. CS outreach queued to 12 account leads, scheduled update in 30m.

ops-bot: Pager events: 1 acknowledgement (maria), 3 assigned (chen, adarsh, lee). escalation policy paused.

maria: thank you. next steps: 1) keep rollback / override for 30m until patch deployed 2) run canary of patched policy on a very small subset (1% routers) with synthetic probes 3) longer term: add additional metric gates for pin-fallthroughs and force pin regression tests 4) postmortem to include timeline, code fix, rollout guard improvements.

chen: PR merged into main (PR #9082) and building. deploying to staging canary now. patch addresses evaluation order and adds a unit test.

adarsh: staging canary passed synthetic probe (10k requests) — no region flip observed. scheduling 1% prod canary at +20m.

maria: monitoring: errors down to 0.4% and falling, latency back to baseline. keeping this thread open until 1h stable.

lee: TTL reverted to 300s after 45m of stability, CDN purges complete. leaving region overrides in place for 60m to ensure no stray cache.

sophia: CS message sent to impacted accounts, templated note attached. flagged for follow-up postmortem content.

maria: thanks all — moving to retrospective: schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 UTC with eng-sre, eng-runtime, networking, devex. I'll file the incident ticket and add timeline + links to logs. closing pages and setting status -> mitigated. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED: root cause identified as policy evaluation ordering bug when latency fallback interacts with pin annotations. mitigation: policy rollback + forced pin overrides + DNS TTL adjustment. follow-up: patch merged (PR #9082), canary scheduled, postmortem required.

maria: closing thread, will attach timeline & artifacts to incident ticket 1725301234.
